skill.name: refactor-code

content.value_statement: Refactoring can improve code but may introduce regressions when changes are broad. This skill guides phased analysis, small edits, tests, rollback planning, and clear reports.
actual_capabilities: Guides branch and issue checks before refactoring work begins.
Structures refactoring proposals with target files, risks, expected benefits, and test plans.
Shows Java refactoring patterns for duplicate code, complex conditions, and N+1 query problems.
Shows TypeScript and React patterns for custom hooks and container-presentational separation.
Directs test, lint, build, unused-code, and server-start checks after changes.
Provides completion and rollback report formats for regression handling.
limitations: The workflow assumes an Orchestrator and Regression Guardian process.
The examples focus on Java backend and TypeScript React frontend code.
It provides instructions and templates, not executable automation scripts.
Project commands must be verified against each repository before use.

use_cases.title: Reduce Technical Debt
use_cases.description: Plan small refactors that remove duplication, simplify logic, and preserve existing behavior.

use_cases.title: Review Refactor Risk
use_cases.description: Create a proposal that explains target files, regression risk, tests, and rollback handling.

use_cases.title: Validate Changes Before Handoff
use_cases.description: Use structured checklists for tests, builds, unused code, server startup, and completion reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Identify Refactor Targets
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of one feature area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature area for simple refactor opportunities. Focus on duplication, naming, complexity, and tests that protect behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Safe Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a refactoring proposal for these files. Include the problem, proposed steps, expected benefit, risk, and verification plan.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Incrementally
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this code in small steps. After each step, explain the behavior preserved, the test impact, and any unused code removed.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Regression and Rollback
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after test or behavior failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this failed refactor. Identify the likely regression cause, recommend rollback or repair, and propose a smaller retry plan.

output_examples.input: A service has repeated authentication checks in several methods.
output_examples.output: A proposal to extract a shared authentication helper, update affected methods, run existing tests, and add focused coverage for unauthorized access.

output_examples.input: A React component mixes fetching, loading state, error handling, and rendering.
output_examples.output: A plan to move data logic into a custom hook and keep the component focused on presentation and state display.

output_examples.input: A refactor caused a failing regression check.
output_examples.output: A rollback-oriented report that records the detected behavior change, suspected cause, executed verification, and smaller follow-up plan.

best_practices: Start with a small scope and record the behavior that must stay unchanged.
Run relevant tests before and after each meaningful refactor step.
Remove unused code and imports created by the refactor before completion.
anti_patterns: Do not combine broad rewrites with feature changes in the same refactor.
Do not change test intent only to make a refactor pass.
Do not skip rollback planning for high-risk logic such as auth, payments, or schema changes.

faq.question: What kind of refactoring does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports safer cleanup of duplication, complex logic, frontend structure, backend performance issues, and unused code.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides recommended local checks that the user or agent must review before running.

faq.question: Which languages are covered by the examples?
faq.answer: The examples focus on Java backend code and TypeScript React frontend code.

faq.question: How does it reduce regression risk?
faq.answer: It uses small steps, baseline checks, test execution, Regression Guardian handoff, and rollback reporting.

faq.question: Can it handle performance refactoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes guidance for N+1 queries, unnecessary loops, memory use, and cache review.

faq.question: Is it tied to one project workflow?
faq.answer: Partly. It references Orchestrator, Regression Guardian, and MovieMarketer conventions that may need adaptation.
